_meta.note: UP ODOP designated products for all 75 districts, transcribed from the official ODOP cell list at odopup.in (district-wise-products). Local 'anchor' descriptors are qualitative cluster/craft context compiled from public sources; no specific figures are fabricated. Applicants must confirm their district's current designated product and scheme terms with the ODOP cell / District Industries Centre before applying.

districts.name: Agra
districts.anchor: Agra is India's largest leather-footwear manufacturing and export hub, supplying a major share of the country's shoe output to domestic and global brands, alongside a marble and stone inlay craft tradition rooted in the city of the Taj.

districts.name: Amroha
districts.anchor: Amroha is renowned for crafting the dholak and other wooden percussion instruments, a specialised handicraft cluster, with a readymade-garment manufacturing base as the district's second ODOP track.

districts.name: Aligarh
districts.anchor: Aligarh is India's lock-making capital, producing the bulk of the country's locks and builder hardware through a very large base of small and micro units, with allied metal-handicraft work.

districts.name: Auraiya
districts.anchor: Auraiya is known for desi-ghee and dairy processing, with a cluster of units leveraging the region's dairy belt to supply ghee and milk products across the area.

districts.name: Azamgarh
districts.anchor: Azamgarh is famed for GI-tagged Nizamabad black pottery — distinctive shiny black clayware with silver-toned patterns — crafted by a heritage potter community in Nizamabad town.

districts.name: Ambedkar Nagar
districts.anchor: Ambedkar Nagar, with Tanda at its centre, is a long-established handloom and textile-products cluster producing cotton cloth through a dense network of looms.

districts.name: Amethi
districts.anchor: Amethi is known for moonj-grass craft — baskets, boxes and decorative articles woven from the grass — a women-led cottage industry in the Awadh belt.

districts.name: Ayodhya
districts.anchor: Ayodhya's ODOP is jaggery (gur), leveraging the local sugarcane belt; the district's pilgrimage economy adds steady demand for traditional food products.

districts.name: Budaun
districts.anchor: Budaun's artisans work in zari-zardozi metallic-thread embroidery, supplying embellished apparel and textiles as part of the wider Rohilkhand embroidery belt.

districts.name: Baghpat
districts.anchor: Baghpat is known for its home-furnishing handloom cluster — bedsheets, furnishings and cotton textiles — with a long weaving tradition serving domestic furnishing markets.

districts.name: Bahraich
districts.anchor: Bahraich is celebrated for its rare wheat-stalk craft — decorative articles made from wheat stems — a distinctive agricultural-by-product handicraft, alongside a food-processing base.

districts.name: Bareilly
districts.anchor: Bareilly is a major zari-zardozi metallic-thread embroidery centre, well known too for cane and bamboo craft and a goldsmith tradition, with a large home-based artisan workforce.

districts.name: Ballia
districts.anchor: Ballia's ODOP centres on bindi (tikuli) making, a cottage craft cluster in eastern UP near the Bihar border producing decorative forehead adornments.

districts.name: Basti
districts.anchor: Basti has a woodcraft cluster producing carved and turned wooden articles, alongside a niche in traditional vinegar products, serving regional markets in eastern UP.

districts.name: Balrampur
districts.anchor: Balrampur has a food-processing cluster around pulses and cereals, adding value to the district's agricultural produce in the Devipatan region.

districts.name: Bhadohi
districts.anchor: Bhadohi — officially Sant Ravidas Nagar — is India's carpet-export capital and the largest hand-knotted carpet and dhurrie weaving cluster in South Asia, with GI-tagged Bhadohi carpets and a weaver base running into the lakhs.

districts.name: Banda
districts.anchor: Banda is famed for GI-tagged Shazar stone — a rare landscape agate found in the Ken river — carved into jewellery and decorative pieces by a small, distinctive artisan community.

districts.name: Bijnor
districts.anchor: Bijnor has a woodcraft cluster producing carved and turned wooden articles and furniture, drawing on the region's long carpentry tradition.

districts.name: Barabanki
districts.anchor: Barabanki is a significant handloom and textile-products cluster near Lucknow, producing woven and printed fabrics with a large weaver base.

districts.name: Bulandshahr
districts.anchor: Bulandshahr is home to Khurja, the GI-tagged 'Ceramic City' — one of India's oldest pottery and glazed-ceramic clusters, supplying crockery, tiles and decorative ceramics nationwide.

districts.name: Chandauli
districts.anchor: Chandauli, near Varanasi, hosts a zari-zardozi embroidery cluster feeding the Banaras textile trade, and is increasingly known for its aromatic black rice as an allied ODOP produce.

districts.name: Chitrakoot
districts.anchor: Chitrakoot produces wooden toys and lacquered wooden articles, a craft cluster tied to the pilgrimage economy and traditional turnery of the Bundelkhand region.

districts.name: Deoria
districts.product: Decorative products, embroidery, weaving & readymade garments
districts.anchor: Deoria's ODOP spans decorative craft, embroidery, weaving and readymade garments — a diversified handicraft and textile cluster serving eastern-UP markets.

districts.name: Etawah
districts.anchor: Etawah has a textile-products, tailoring and garment-embroidery cluster producing readymade items and embellished apparel for central-UP markets.

districts.name: Etah
districts.anchor: Etah is known for bell-metal craft — ghungroo (ankle bells), temple bells and allied brass articles — a specialised metalworking cluster with a long casting tradition.

districts.name: Farrukhabad
districts.anchor: Farrukhabad is a noted hand-block-printing centre, producing block-printed fabrics, bedsheets and furnishings with traditional wooden blocks, alongside zari-zardozi work.

districts.name: Fatehpur
districts.anchor: Fatehpur pairs a bedsheet and home-furnishing textile cluster with an iron-fabrication trade, producing cotton furnishings and fabricated metal goods for regional distribution.

districts.name: Firozabad
districts.anchor: Firozabad is the 'Glass City' (Suhag Nagri), the heart of India's glass-bangle and glassware industry, with thousands of furnaces producing bangles, decorative glass and laboratory glassware.

districts.name: Gautam Buddh Nagar
districts.anchor: Gautam Buddh Nagar (Noida) is a large readymade-garment and apparel manufacturing and export hub within the NCR, hosting numerous units serving domestic retail and export buyers.

districts.name: Ghazipur
districts.anchor: Ghazipur is known for jute wall-hangings and jute craft, turning the fibre into decorative furnishings through a cottage-craft cluster in eastern UP.

districts.name: Ghaziabad
districts.anchor: Ghaziabad, on the NCR industrial belt, is a major engineering-goods cluster producing machinery, components and fabricated products with strong logistics connectivity to Delhi.

districts.name: Gonda
districts.anchor: Gonda's ODOP is food processing centred on pulses and cereals, with units adding value to the district's substantial agricultural produce.

districts.name: Gorakhpur
districts.anchor: Gorakhpur is famed for GI-tagged Gorakhpur terracotta — the painted clay figures and pottery of Aurangabad village — a heritage potter craft, with a readymade-garment base as a second track.

districts.name: Hapur
districts.anchor: Hapur hosts a home-furnishing cluster producing textiles and furnishings, with a base of small manufacturing units serving the western-UP and NCR markets.

districts.name: Hardoi
districts.anchor: Hardoi has a handloom and dari (floor-covering) weaving cluster producing cotton furnishings and woven fabrics for the Awadh-region market.

districts.name: Hathras
districts.anchor: Hathras is India's principal asafoetida (hing) processing and trading centre, where raw resin is processed into the spice and distributed across the country.

districts.name: Hamirpur
districts.anchor: Hamirpur's ODOP centres on footwear and shoe craft, with a cluster of small units producing leather and synthetic footwear for regional markets in Bundelkhand.

districts.name: Jalaun
districts.anchor: Jalaun, centred on Kalpi, is famed for GI-tagged handmade paper — one of India's oldest handmade-paper clusters producing craft and art papers from cotton rag and recycled fibre.

districts.name: Jaunpur
districts.anchor: Jaunpur is known for woollen and cotton durrie (dari) weaving, a floor-covering handloom cluster with a long weaving heritage in eastern UP.

districts.name: Jhansi
districts.anchor: Jhansi's ODOP is soft toys, with a growing cluster of stitching and stuffing units producing plush toys for domestic retail across the Bundelkhand region.

districts.name: Kaushambi
districts.anchor: Kaushambi, a major banana-growing belt, has a banana food-processing and fibre-craft base, turning the crop and its by-products into processed foods and decorative articles.

districts.name: Kannauj
districts.anchor: Kannauj is India's 'Perfume Capital', home to the GI-tagged Kannauj attar (ittar) — traditional steam-distilled natural perfume — with a distillation industry stretching back centuries.

districts.name: Kushinagar
districts.anchor: Kushinagar, a banana-growing belt and Buddhist pilgrimage site, has a banana-fibre craft cluster making mats, bags and decorative articles from the fibre.

districts.name: Kanpur Dehat
districts.anchor: Kanpur Dehat hosts a cluster of aluminium utensil and cookware units supplying household and commercial kitchenware, building on the greater Kanpur industrial belt's metalworking base.

districts.name: Kanpur Nagar
districts.anchor: Kanpur is a historic leather-tanning and finished-goods centre — once the 'Manchester of the East' — with a large tannery and saddlery cluster along the Ganga and a significant leather-export footprint.

districts.name: Kasganj
districts.anchor: Kasganj hosts a zari-zardozi metallic-thread craft cluster supplying embellishment work and embroidered textiles to the western-UP apparel trade.

districts.name: Lakhimpur Kheri
districts.anchor: Lakhimpur Kheri, with its Tharu tribal belt near the Dudhwa forests, is known for Tharu tribal craft and handloom, alongside jaggery production from the local sugarcane belt.

districts.name: Lalitpur
districts.anchor: Lalitpur has a zari-silk handloom cluster in the Bundelkhand region producing woven saris in a Chanderi-influenced tradition, plus a readymade-garment and hosiery base.

districts.name: Lucknow
districts.anchor: Lucknow is the home of GI-tagged Chikankari, the delicate hand-embroidery tradition, alongside zardozi metallic-thread work; the craft sustains a very large, predominantly women, artisan base.

districts.name: Maharajganj
districts.anchor: Maharajganj, with forest-belt timber access, has a furniture and woodcraft cluster producing wooden furniture and carved articles for regional markets.

districts.name: Meerut
districts.anchor: Meerut is one of India's principal sports-goods manufacturing hubs, producing cricket bats, balls and a wide range of sporting equipment for national and international markets.

districts.name: Mahoba
districts.anchor: Mahoba is known for Gaura-stone craft — carved articles from the locally quarried soft stone — a distinctive Bundelkhand stone-working cluster.

districts.name: Mirzapur
districts.anchor: Mirzapur, part of the historic carpet belt alongside Bhadohi, is a major hand-knotted carpet and dhurrie weaving cluster with deep export linkages, plus an allied brass industry.

districts.name: Mainpuri
districts.anchor: Mainpuri is famed for GI-tagged Tarkashi — intricate brass-wire inlay on wood — a heritage craft producing decorative articles through a small but distinctive artisan community.

districts.name: Moradabad
districts.anchor: Moradabad is 'Peetal Nagri' (Brass City), India's leading brass-handicraft export cluster with GI-tagged metal craft, exporting decorative and utility brassware worldwide.

districts.name: Mathura
districts.anchor: Mathura hosts a manufacturing cluster spanning sanitary fittings and temple craft — costumes, shringar articles and kanthi mala for the Thakur Ji tradition — driven by the city's pilgrimage economy.

districts.name: Muzaffarnagar
districts.anchor: Muzaffarnagar sits in UP's sugarcane heartland and is one of India's largest jaggery (gur) producing and trading centres, with a vast network of khandsari and gur-processing units.

districts.name: Mau
districts.anchor: Mau is a major powerloom-textile centre producing saris and dress material, with thousands of looms forming one of eastern UP's densest weaving clusters.

districts.name: Pilibhit
districts.anchor: Pilibhit is celebrated as India's flute (bansuri) manufacturing hub, exporting bamboo flutes across the country and abroad, alongside a wooden-products craft base.

districts.name: Prayagraj
districts.anchor: Prayagraj is known for moonj-grass craft — baskets, boxes and decorative articles woven from moonj and kaasa grass — a women-led cottage craft cluster.

districts.name: Pratapgarh
districts.anchor: Pratapgarh is India's amla (Indian gooseberry) heartland, with a food-processing cluster turning amla into candy, murabba, juice and allied products.

districts.name: Raebareli
districts.anchor: Raebareli has a woodcraft and furniture cluster producing carved and turned wooden articles for the Awadh-region market.

districts.name: Rampur
districts.anchor: Rampur is known for applique and patchwork and zari-patchwork embroidery, alongside being a major mentha (mint) producing and processing belt.

districts.name: Sant Kabir Nagar
districts.anchor: Sant Kabir Nagar hosts a brassware-craft cluster producing utensils and decorative metalware, linked to the eastern-UP metalworking tradition.

districts.name: Shahjahanpur
districts.anchor: Shahjahanpur has a zari-zardozi embroidery cluster producing embellished textiles, part of the wider Rohilkhand embroidery tradition.

districts.name: Shamli
districts.anchor: Shamli hosts an iron-arts and fabrication cluster producing agricultural implements, fasteners and decorative ironwork for the western-UP farming belt.

districts.name: Saharanpur
districts.anchor: Saharanpur is renowned for GI-tagged intricate wood carving in sheesham, supplying carved furniture, panels and decorative items to domestic and export markets.

districts.name: Shravasti
districts.anchor: Shravasti's ODOP centres on tribal craft and decorative articles, a niche handicraft cluster tied to the district's heritage and pilgrimage footfall.

districts.name: Sambhal
districts.anchor: Sambhal specialises in horn-and-bone handicraft, an export-oriented niche craft turning animal by-product into decorative and utility articles for international buyers.

districts.name: Siddharthnagar
districts.anchor: Siddharthnagar is the home of GI-tagged Kalanamak rice, an aromatic black-husked heritage rice linked to the Buddha, with a dedicated cultivation and processing cluster.

districts.name: Sitapur
districts.anchor: Sitapur is a leading cotton-dari (durrie) weaving centre, producing floor coverings and furnishings through a large weaving cluster supplying national markets.

districts.name: Sonbhadra
districts.anchor: Sonbhadra, in the carpet-and-mineral belt of south-eastern UP, has a carpet-weaving cluster drawing on the regional weaving tradition.

districts.name: Sultanpur
districts.anchor: Sultanpur has a moonj-grass craft cluster producing woven baskets and decorative articles, a women-led cottage industry in the Awadh region.

districts.name: Unnao
districts.anchor: Unnao hosts a zari-zardozi embroidery cluster between Kanpur and Lucknow, plus a leather-products trade linked to the neighbouring Kanpur leather belt.

districts.name: Varanasi
districts.anchor: Varanasi is famed for the GI-tagged Banarasi silk sari, a centuries-old handloom brocade tradition supporting a very large weaver community and one of India's most recognised handloom names.
